title: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)
what_it_is: Committee of Supply – Head I (Ministry of Social and Family Development)

sections.label: Budget cut motion on social mobility
sections.summary: A motion is moved to reduce Head I of the Estimates by $100, after speeches on social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Chairman, I move, "That the total sum allocated to Head I of the Estimates be reduced by $100." Members on both sides of the House have spoken passionately in this House about social mobility in Singapore.

sections.label: Slowing relative social mobility in Singapore
sections.summary: Relative social mobility in Singapore has been slowing, with fewer bottom-quintile earners reaching the top and more staying at the bottom.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: There would be an equal chance, basically, of moving up to the top, or anywhere in between, or remaining at the bottom, in an ideal world.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, in Singapore,13.8% of those born into the bottom 20% in the 1985 to 1989 cohorts made it to the top 20% of earners while 25.3% ended up in the bottom 20% of earners, like their fathers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Compared to the 1978 to 1982 cohorts, in other words, those born just seven years earlier, the 1985 to 1989 cohorts have almost one full percentage point less that made it to the top 20% of earners, and one full percentage point more that ended up in the same bottom 20%, like their fathers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: So, relative social mobility in Singapore has been slowing even as we sustained broad-based progress for all.

sections.label: Closing opportunities gap not government alone
sections.summary: Keeping relative social mobility alive and containing the opportunities gap cannot be left to the Government or social sector alone.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Keeping relative social mobility alive, essentially, containing that opportunities gap between your children and mine, almost by definition, cannot be left to the Government, or for that matter, the social sector, alone.

sections.label: Call for longitudinal social mobility research
sections.summary: The speaker calls for longitudinal research on mechanisms driving social mobility at the individual level, beyond descriptive correlations.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Ms Sylvia Lim, in the same speech in 2018, called for longitudinal studies that will, "track the fate of families (at the bottom) over time" and indeed, go "beyond numbers to dig deep into the daily lives and evaluate the reasons why they do not seem to be able to catch up with the rest of society." MOF's Occasional Papers in 2015 and 2025 do provide a longitudinal view on how families at the bottom are doing.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: To really help us in our work to close the opportunities gap throughout life and keep relative social mobility alive in Singapore, I think we need longitudinal research in Singapore that goes beyond descriptive correlations amongst group averages, to mechanisms that elucidate what actually drives social mobility, at the individual level and models that can predict and simulate how social mobility might change with certain shifts to the drivers of mobility, again at the individual level.

sections.label: Urging investment in longitudinal dataset
sections.summary: The Government is urged to construct and invest in a longitudinal dataset enabling models on what drives social mobility.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: But the kind of research being contemplated will need much more than administrative data.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: I urge the Government to consider constructing such a dataset, investing in such a longitudinal dataset, with a view to enabling models that will truly transform our understanding of what drives social mobility, what interventions targeting what drivers may work and work to what extent.

sections.label: Interlocking solutions at scale
sections.summary: A system of interlocking solutions across multiple domains is needed, along with good solutions at scale rather than pilots.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Instead, we need a system of interlocking solutions, across multiple domains – academic, non-academic, social capital formation, financial stability, housing, health – each solution working alongside the others, to collectively close the opportunities gap.

sentences.speaker: Mr Xie Yao Quan (Jurong Central)
sentences.text: Second, we need good solutions at scale, more than excellent pilots that remain as pilots.

sections.label: TOUCH Community Services workers listed
sections.summary: Six social workers and one accountant from TOUCH Community Services share the same Bukit Merah Central address, email and phone number.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Six social workers and one accountant from TOUCH Community Services are listed individually: same address at Bukit Merah Central, same email, same phone number.

sections.label: Donees of last resort question
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether MSF will amend section 12 for accredited organisations and whether Singapore's Public Guardian could be donee of last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: They charge modest fees and provide the option of being donees of last resort.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: I ask, will MSF consider amending section 12 to allow accredited organisations to serve as personal welfare donees?

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: Beyond that, could Singapore's Public Guardian serve as donee of last resort, as Australian states have done?

sections.label: Foreigner registration fee questioned
sections.summary: The registration fee for non-citizens and non-permanent residents is fixed at $230, and the speaker says the public guardian should not apply one blanket fee to all foreigners.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The registration fee for non-citizens and non-permanent residents is currently fixed at $230.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim (Aljunied)
sentences.text: The public guardian should not have a blanket registration fee for all foreigners, which applies to our high-wage Employment Pass (EP) holders and low-wage foreign work permit holders alike.

sections.label: Single parents and dual-family baseline
sections.summary: The framework is largely designed around a dual-family baseline, and single parents often qualify for support only after strict income thresholds.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: While MSF provides assistance schemes, much of the framework remains largely designed around a dual-family baseline.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Single parents often qualify for support only after meeting strict income thresholds and many fall into a financially squeezed middle, earning too much for sustained assistance, yet too little to comfortably manage rising costs.

sections.label: Review of family policy assumptions
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister to clarify whether MSF will review family policy assumptions, outcome metrics and inter-Ministry coordination.

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: And if so, does that sufficiently reflect current realities, including single-parent households, blended families, delayed marriages and dual-career pressures?

sentences.speaker: Mr Gabriel Lam (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I would therefore like the Minister to clarify whether MSF intends to undertake a broader review of family policy design assumptions; whether outcome metrics for "family strength" go beyond programme uptake to measure stability, financial resilience and child well-being across diverse household types; and whether inter-Ministry coordination, particularly with the Ministry of Manpower, Ministry of National Development and Ministry of Education, is being strengthened to address root pressures embedded in our housing, labour and education systems, rather than relying primarily on awareness campaigns.

sections.label: Unwed parents excluded from benefits
sections.summary: Unwed parents do not receive the Baby Bonus cash gift and are not eligible for tax benefits such as Working Mother's Child Relief and Parenthood Tax Rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: Currently, unwed parents do not receive the Baby Bonus cash gift, and they are not eligible for tax benefits, such as the Working Mother's Child Relief and the Parenthood Tax Rebate.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye (Radin Mas)
sentences.text: These differences can have a real impact, especially for lower-income single parent households.

sections.label: Li Hwan childcare centre closure
sections.summary: Li Hwan centre announced closure in January; 52 parents rallied, two took it over, but full-day fees are $1,655 monthly with no Government funding, while a nearby POP centre charges $650.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: In January this year, her Li Hwan centre announced closure; 52 parents rallied to save it.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: Two of them, Nicole and Jasmine, believed enough in the school to take it over themselves.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: But the structural challenge remains – full-day fees are $1,655 a month, with no Government funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat
sentences.text: The Partner Operator (POP) centre nearby charges $650.

sections.label: Workers' Party leave proposals
sections.summary: The Workers' Party recommends extending childcare leave per child up to age 12 and establishing paid family care leave for those caring for elderly parents or severely disabled family members.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: The Workers' Party recommends extending childcare leave on a per child basis up to age 12.

sentences.speaker: Ms Eileen Chong Pei Shan (Non-Constituency Member)
sentences.text: We also propose establishing paid family care leave for Singaporeans with primary caregiving responsibilities for elderly parents or family members with severe disabilities.

sections.label: Adoption and baby trafficking
sections.summary: Adoptions should be encouraged, but Indonesia's investigation into an alleged baby trafficking ring supplying Singapore is concerning; Andre Low filed a Parliamentary Question on ASEAN cooperation, and Minister Masagos cited the ASEAN Regional Plan of Action 2016-2025.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: Adoptions should be encouraged, not just for the wholehearted act of love that it embodies but also to mitigate our dismal total fertility rate.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: It is thus very concerning to receive news of investigations by Indonesia into an alleged baby trafficking ring supplying babies to Singapore for adoption.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In November 2025, Workers' Party Non-constituency Member Andre Low filed a Parliamentary Question about regional cooperation among the Association of Southeast Asian Nations (ASEAN) countries to protect against child trafficking in inter-country adoptions.

sentences.speaker: Ms Sylvia Lim
sentences.text: In answer, MSF Minister Masagos mentioned the ASEAN Regional Plan of Action on the Elimination of Violence against Children from 2016 to 2025.

sections.label: Foster and institutionalised children numbers
sections.summary: The speaker has three foster kids including a toddler, and about 500 plus children are under fostering and 500 plus under institutions, which is not a good place to be.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: I have three foster kids with me, including one toddler.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: There are about 500 plus children under fostering and the 500 plus under institutions, which is really not a good place to be.

sections.label: Foster children information access issues
sections.summary: Foster children face issues accessing information: they cannot access the school portal and cannot book online medical appointments.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: But there are really issues on the information access for the foster kids.

sentences.speaker: Dr Neo Kok Beng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: They cannot access the school portal and they cannot book online medical.

sections.label: Mandatory co-parenting programmes support
sections.summary: The speaker supports the policy intent behind mandatory co-parenting programmes for divorcing couples with children below 21 years old.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: In that regard, I support the policy intent behind the mandatory co-parenting programmes for divorcing couples with children below 21 years old.

sections.label: Counselling session booking waits
sections.summary: The speaker notes physical counselling sessions take weeks to book, with longer waits during festive periods and at heavily subscribed Family Service Centres.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Chairman, I make two observations on how MSF can improve this in a practical way.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I was informed that the physical counselling session take weeks to book, with longer waits during festive periods and at more heavily subscribed Family Service Centre locations.

sections.label: Gap in who must attend
sections.summary: The speaker says there appears to be a gap in who is required to attend the programme if its purpose is protecting children through co-parenting readiness.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Next, Chairman, if the programme's purpose is to protect children by improving co-parenting readiness, there appears to be a gap in who is required to attend.

sections.label: Domestic child abduction response
sections.summary: The speaker urges treating domestic child abduction as time-critical, citing no rapid response track and proposing indicators, an expedited judicial pathway and operational support.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: While international child abduction triggers urgent return mechanisms under the Hague Convention, domestic removals within Singapore do not have an equivalent rapid response track, leaving left-behind parents to wait for months whilst their applications are being resolved in Court.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: Yet for the child, the harm caused by sudden separation can be just as real and just as lasting.

sentences.speaker: Ms Diana Pang Li Yen (Marine Parade-Braddell Heights)
sentences.text: I therefore urge that we treat domestic child abduction as a time-critical child welfare issue by tracking and publishing core indicators and by creating an expedited judicial pathway with early neutral review, swift restoration of safe interim contact where appropriate, proportionate deterrence against bad-faith conduct by one parent and all-round operational support for parents, so that we protect genuine safety cases while preventing abuse of a "remove first, explain later" tactic and safeguarding children's best interests.

sections.label: Recognising caregiving as real work
sections.summary: The speaker says a society putting "we first" must recognise caregiving as real work, naming single parents, families with special needs children and mid-career caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: A society that puts "we first", must recognise caregiving as real work – whether it is a single parent balancing work and childcare, families raising children with special needs who juggle between therapy appointments and education, or mid-career workers caring for elderly parents while trying to remain economically active.

sections.label: Integrated support for caregivers
sections.summary: The speaker asks the Minister how MSF is strengthening integrated support services for caregivers.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As such, can the Minister share how MSF is strengthening integrated support services for caregivers?

sections.label: Caseload sustainability and officer wellbeing
sections.summary: The speaker asks how the Ministry ensures caseload sustainability, officers' career development, upskilling, mental wellbeing and reduced burnout risk amid digitalisation.

sentences.speaker: Mr Sanjeev Kumar Tiwari (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: As the Ministry advances digitalisation and service transformation, how is it ensuring caseload sustainability, safeguarding officers' career development and upskilling, mental wellbeing and mitigating risks of burnout, so that the social services sector remains a rewarding and sustainable career for officers?

sections.label: ComLink+ milestones and payouts
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Budget enhancements to ComLink+ and asks how new milestones will be calibrated and enhanced payouts reflect sustained efforts.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: This can dampen motivation and affect take up, particularly among those who already find the journey daunting.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: I therefore welcome this year's enhancements to ComLink+, including new payouts, smaller, but more achievable milestones and cash incentives.

sentences.speaker: Mr Melvin Yong Yik Chye
sentences.text: Could the Ministry share more details on how these new milestones will be calibrated and how the enhanced payouts will better reflect sustained efforts?

sections.label: Screen time outside school
sections.summary: The Government banned smartphones in secondary schools, but excessive screen time outside school hours remains a challenge, especially for lower-income children.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: While the Government has banned smartphone use in secondary schools, excessive screen time outside school hours remains a challenge, especially for children from lower-income families.

sections.label: ComLink+ support needs engagement
sections.summary: The speaker says Budget 2026 strengthens support for ComLink+ families, but its effectiveness relies entirely on successful engagement.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, while Budget 2026 rightly strengthens support for ComLink+ families, the effectiveness of this support relies entirely on successful engagement.

sections.label: Budget 2026 ComLink+ enhancements
sections.summary: The speaker welcomes Budget 2026 enhancements including higher cash payouts, intermediate milestones, higher caps and a new $500 quarterly Partnership Payout.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: When support is integrated, milestones are clear and progress is sustained, families do not only cope, they move forward.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: I welcome the enhancements in Budget 2026 – higher cash payouts tied to stable employment and preschool attendance, intermediate milestones, higher caps and the new $500 quarterly Partnership Payout.

sections.label: One shared progression plan
sections.summary: The speaker asks whether agencies could move towards one shared progression plan with one dashboard, one set of goals and one coordinated journey.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Could we move towards one shared progression plan across agencies – one dashboard, one set of goals, one coordinated journey?

sections.label: Measure transformation not transactions
sections.summary: The speaker says to measure transformation, not transactions, including jobs retained, sustained preschool attendance, reduced debt and stabilised stress.

sentences.speaker: Ms Mariam Jaafar (Sembawang)
sentences.text: Fourth, measure transformation, not transactions – not just payouts issued, but job retained, sustained preschool attendance, debt reduced, stress stabilised.

sections.label: Disability spending front-loaded to childhood
sections.summary: Disability spending is front-loaded towards childhood while adult services operate under very tight margins despite adulthood lasting 60 years or more.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, disability spending today is front-loaded towards childhood while adult services operate under very tight margins even though adulthood can last 60 years or more.

sections.label: Base funding and means-tested subsidies
sections.summary: It proposes a universal base funding component for every DAC or residential home client, plus means-tested subsidies on top for affordability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: First, provide a universal base funding component for every client served by a DAC or residential home.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: Second, on top of this base, apply a means-tested subsidies to ensure affordability for families who need them.

sections.label: National disability job redesign fund
sections.summary: The task force should consider a national disability job redesign fund to identify at-risk jobs, surface new jobs, redesign workflows and strengthen job-coach capability.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: The task force should consider a national disability job redesign fund to support the identification of jobs at risk, surface new jobs in the new economy, redesign workflows to allow PwDs who can contribute and strengthen job-coach capability.

sections.label: Family life navigator model
sections.summary: For families with higher needs, it proposes a family life navigator model similar to the family coach approach in ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Ms Denise Phua Lay Peng (Jalan Besar)
sentences.text: For families with higher needs, introduce a family life navigator model, similar to the family coach approach in ComLink+.

sections.label: Waiting causes regression and caregiver stress
sections.summary: Waiting months or years for placement causes regression, desocialisation and isolation, shifting care burden onto families and leading to caregiver stress, exhaustion, anxiety and depression.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: Waiting months or years for placement is not just a logistical delay, it results in regression in skills, desocialisation and isolation, and shifts the full burden of care back onto families, often leading to chronic stress, physical exhaustion and even anxiety and depression among caregivers.

sections.label: Aggressive expansion to eliminate waiting times
sections.summary: It argues 500 additional DAC places by 2030 will not meet demand and calls for aggressive facility expansion and eliminating waiting times altogether.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It would be unthinkable if this happened to our normal school-going students, and yet we expect families with special needs children to wait when we know that the need for predictable schedules is especially important in this group.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We will soon be adding another 3,000 SPED school places by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We would not be doing so if the demand was not there.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: So, while it has been announced that another 500 DAC places will be available by 2030, I firmly believe that this will not even come close to fulfilling the actual demand.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: It seems like we are perpetually trying to play catch up to a gap in services that is only getting wider.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: We need an aggressive expansion of facilities and a commitment to eliminate waiting times altogether.

sections.label: DAC fees for high support needs
sections.summary: Current fees at disability care centres remain unaffordable to many in the sandwiched class despite means-tested subsidies.

sentences.speaker: Ms Kuah Boon Theng (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For DACs who cater to those with high support needs, even with present means-tested subsidies, the current fees would still be unaffordable to many in the sandwiched class.

sections.label: Longer lives for persons with disabilities
sections.summary: Persons with disabilities are living significantly longer due to medical advances, with Down syndrome life expectancy about 60 years.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: First, persons with disabilities are living significantly longer due to advances in medical care.

sentences.speaker: Prof Kenneth Poon (Nominated Member)
sentences.text: For example, a local report by the Community Health Outreach for Wellness in 2024 indicates that individuals with Down syndrome now have a life expectancy of about 60 years.

sections.label: SMU survey on employability awareness
sections.summary: An SMU survey found eight in 10 PwDs had never heard of employability training and fewer than half of employers knew of grants.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: A recent Singapore Management University (SMU) survey found that eight in 10 PwDs had never heard of employability training programmes and fewer than half of employers were aware of workplace grants and hiring incentives.

sections.label: PwD employment rate and taskforce
sections.summary: Over 30% of PwDs are employed with a roadmap to 40% by 2030, and a taskforce will act on employment, community living and affordability.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: Today, more than 30% of PwDs are in employment, with a roadmap to move up to 40% by 2030.

sentences.speaker: Mr Ng Chee Meng (Jalan Kayu)
sentences.text: The Taskforce on Assurance for Families with Persons with Disabilities will also be doing more in three key areas: employment, community living and affordability.

sections.label: Sign language counselling access
sections.summary: Few counsellors are trained in Singapore Sign Language, so deaf clients rely on interpreters, limiting privacy and help-seeking.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Chairman, today, very few counsellors are trained in Singapore Sign Language.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Thus, deaf clients often rely on interpreters from an already small community.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: This often limits privacy and discourage self and help-seeking.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: In countries, such as Canada, sign-language counselling is provided as a standard service.

sentences.speaker: Miss Rachel Ong
sentences.text: Will MSF review funding and support schemes to ensure Singapore Sign Language interpretation is systematically available across counselling, social support centres and crisis response services, so deaf Singaporeans can access help confidentially and equitably?

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: MSF aims to foster a Singapore society where all families are supported at every stage of their life to thrive on their terms.

sections.label: Social health integration model trial
sections.summary: In 2025, MSF trialed the social health integration model with MOH for ComLink+ families to address health barriers to social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 2025, MSF trialed the social health integration model with MOH for ComLink+ families to ensure that health challenges do not hinder their social mobility.

sections.label: Healthier SG ComLink+ enrolment extension
sections.summary: From 2027, MOH will extend Healthier SG enrolment to eligible ComLink+ residents aged 25 to 39.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: From 2027, MOH will extend Healthier SG enrolment to eligible ComLink+ residents age 25 to 39.

sections.label: Co-parenting programme for divorcing couples
sections.summary: Since July 2024, all couples with minor children must attend the co-parenting programme before filing for divorce.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Since July 2024, all couples with minor children must go through the co-parenting programme run by Strengthening Family Programme centres, and that is before they filed for divorce.

sections.label: Doubling caseload by 2030
sections.summary: By 2030, 12,000 cases will be served, double today's caseload.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: By 2030, we will be able to serve 12,000 cases, double of today's caseload.

sections.label: Sustainable Philanthropy Framework and DBS pledge
sections.summary: In 2024, MSF and NCSS launched the Sustainable Philanthropy Framework, with DBS pledging up to $1 billion and 1.5 million volunteer hours.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: In 2024, MSF and National Council of Social Service (NCSS) launched the Sustainable Philanthropy Framework to encourage corporates to integrate social impact with their business goals and engage in more consistent giving and volunteering.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For instance, DBS has pledged up to $1 billion and 1.5 million employee volunteer hours over the next decade to better support those with less means, including $6.5 million to KidSTART, and $30 million to the ComLink+ Progress Packages.

sections.label: Longitudinal study on social mobility
sections.summary: MSF agreed to Mr Xie's call for longitudinal research and collaborated with IPS on a study on social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Mr Xie called for longitudinal research to understand better the drivers of social mobility.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: We agree, which is why we have collaborated with the IPS on a longitudinal study called Pathways and Trajectories of Households in Singapore to better understand this.

sections.label: Capability Exchange Programme launch
sections.summary: Last month, the Capability Exchange Programme was launched for learning and exchanges among government officials and practitioners.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Last month, we launched the Capability Exchange Programme to create opportunities for learning and exchanges among government officials and practitioners from these countries.

sections.label: Sabbatical Leave Scheme for social service professionals
sections.summary: Eligible social service professionals may use the Sabbatical Leave Scheme for 10 weeks of paid leave to recharge and refresh.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Eligible social service professionals may also tap on the Sabbatical Leave Scheme, which gives them 10 weeks of paid leave to recharge and refresh.

sections.label: Digitalisation and AI in Youth Homes
sections.summary: Youth Homes digitalised paperwork and file cross-referencing under the Home Central Information System, and officers use AI tools like Pair and AIBots for first drafts.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: For example, in our Youth Homes, time-consuming processes such as filling out paperwork and cross-referencing files are now digitalised under the Home Central Information System.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Officers also use AI tools such as Pair and AIBots that generate first drafts to help officers work more efficiently.

sections.label: Assistive technology and Enabling Lives Initiative funding
sections.summary: Subsidies under the Assistive Technology Fund help persons with disabilities buy assistive devices, and the Enabling Lives Initiative Grant funds AI solutions for independence and employment.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Subsidies are provided to persons with disabilities under the Assistive Technology Fund to purchase assistive technology devices to enable independent living.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Under the Enabling Lives Initiative Grant, funding is also provided to support AI solutions that improve independence and expand employment opportunities for persons with disabilities.

sections.label: Donations to Community Chest and others
sections.summary: Since SG Gives launched last year, over $100 million in donations went to the Community Chest, President's Challenge and the Collective for a Stronger Society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: Together, we have been able to make strides in nurturing resilient individuals, strong families and a caring society.

sentences.speaker: The Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Masagos Zulkifli B M M)
sentences.text: I am heartened that since the launch of SG Gives last year, we have seen over $100 million in donations made to the Community Chest, President's Challenge and the Collective for a Stronger Society.

sections.label: Enhanced ComLink+ Progress Packages payouts
sections.summary: As announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in his Budget speech, ComLink+ Progress Packages are enhanced this year, with all ComLink+ families receiving a new $500 quarterly payout.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: With that, as announced by Prime Minister Lawrence Wong in his Budget speech, we are enhancing the ComLink+ Progress Packages this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: First, all ComLink+ families will now receive a new payout of $500 each quarter.

sections.label: Employment assessed on whole family
sections.summary: For employment, the whole family's efforts will be looked at rather than each person's income.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: For employment, we will look at the whole family's efforts, rather than the income of each person.

sections.label: ComLink+ family payouts
sections.summary: A ComLink+ family with two preschool-aged children can receive up to $10,000 yearly, with more in cash and some in CPF and CDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: Overall, a ComLink+ family with two preschool-aged children can receive up to $10,000 every year by maintaining a household income of at least $2,000 and regular preschool attendance.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: More of the payout will be in cash to better support families facing day-to-day cashflow challenges.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: At the same time, a portion will continue to be placed in families' Central Provident Fund (CPF) and Child Development Accounts (CDA), so that we support not just today's needs but also tomorrow's security.

sections.label: Enablers to bridge employment
sections.summary: Three enhancements will be put in place: facilitate job matching, enable upskilling and support caregiving.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: Even with a stable job, they may need certain educational qualifications or skills to unlock higher wages.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: We will therefore put in place more enablers to bridge the gap to employment, starting with three enhancements: facilitate job matching, enable upskilling and support caregiving.

sections.label: ComLink+ Skills Upgrading Support Pilot
sections.summary: MSF observed upskilling deterrence and rolled out a ComLink+ Skills Upgrading Support Pilot this January.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: MSF has observed that this deters some ComLink+ families from upskilling even when they want to do so and even when they have the opportunity to do so.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: That is why we rolled out a ComLink+ Skills Upgrading Support Pilot this January.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance threshold
sections.summary: MSF will increase the Student Care Fee Assistance income threshold from $4,500 to $6,500 and update income tiers.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: As announced by the Prime Minister in his Budget speech, MSF will increase the Student Care Fee Assistance income threshold from $4,500 to $6,500 and update the income tiers.

sections.label: Student Care Fee Assistance changes
sections.summary: Eligible parents get in-principle approval guaranteeing assistance on enrolment, and the maximum assistance period extends from 24 to 36 months.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: Eligible parents will be granted in-principle approval, which guarantees that they will receive Student Care Fee Assistance once they enrol in an eligible centre.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: We are also extending the maximum Student Care Fee Assistance assistance period from 24 months to 36 months.

sections.label: Partners supporting ComLink+ packages
sections.summary: MSF thanks partners like the DBS Foundation, a strong supporter of ComLink+ progress packages for preschool and homeownership.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: Because truly, it takes a whole-of-society effort to uplift each other.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: We thank our partners for working closely with MSF, like the DBS Foundation, which has been a strong supporter of the ComLink+ progress packages for preschool and homeownership.

sections.label: MSF family support enhancements
sections.summary: MSF will enhance ComLink+ Progress Packages, raise Student Care Fee Assistance income criteria to $6,500, and expand employment support for low-income families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: MSF is committed to supporting every family that needs help so they can achieve stability, self-reliance and progress.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: We will therefore enhance the ComLink+ Progress Packages to ensure more families can get the support they need for their next steps.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: MSF will also boost after-school care support by raising the income criteria for Student Care Fee Assistance from $4,500 to $6,500.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: More than 13,000 students and their families will benefit.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim)
sentences.text: MSF has strengthened collaboration with them, particularly in expanding employment support and skills development opportunities for low-income families.

sections.label: SPED graduates employment outcomes
sections.summary: About 250 SPED graduates each year move into employment or further studies within six months of graduation.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Each year, about 250 SPED graduates move into employment or further studies within six months of graduation.

sections.label: DAC and SW places
sections.summary: A further 520 DAC and 360 SW spaces will come on stream progressively by 2027, addressing long wait times.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: She can go to work knowing that Mirza is safe and meaningfully engaged, and treasures coming home to hear his story about the day.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: But we know the current wait time, from referral to enrolment, is long, over half a year on average.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Our pledge was to add 500 DAC and 500 SW places by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: A further 520 DAC and 360 SW spaces will come on stream progressively by 2027.

sections.label: Clients transitioned to ESLP
sections.summary: As of January this year, close to 770 clients across eight centres have transitioned to ESLP.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: As of January this year, close to 770 clients across eight centres have transitioned to ESLP, and we will continue refining the service model over the next three years.

sections.label: Home Support Programme launch
sections.summary: The Home Support Programme will launch in the second half of this year, extending support to those living independently near ELP sites.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Living side by side, contributing to the same community.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We will also launch the Home Support Programme in the second half of this year, extending similar support to those already living independently or has plans to do so in their homes, near ELP sites.

sections.label: Disability service subsidy increases
sections.summary: From July 2026, subsidies for residential and community disability services will rise, with income threshold raised to per capita income of $3,601 to $4,800.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From July 2026, we will increase subsidies for residential and community disability services by up to 15 and 10 percentage points respectively.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The income threshold for subsidies will also be raised, extending eligibility to households with per capita income between $3,601 and $4,800.

sections.label: MRSS CPF top-up matching
sections.summary: Under the MRSS, CPF top-ups are dollar-matched for eligible persons, up to $2,000 yearly and $20,000 lifetime.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Under the MRSS, we dollar-match CPF top-ups for those eligible, up to an annual cap of $2,000 and a lifetime limit of $20,000.

sections.label: SNT matching top-ups sign-up
sections.summary: From 1 April this year to 31 March 2031, families with per capita household income up to $3,600 can sign up for SNT matching top-ups of up to $10,000.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: From 1 April this year till 31 March 2031, families with per capita household income of up to $3,600 can sign up to receive matching top-ups of up to $10,000 to the SNT accounts.

sections.label: Case Managers and SNT plans
sections.summary: Social work-trained Case Managers work with caregivers on personalised care plans and ensure funds are disbursed per plans after caregivers pass; with Community Chest sponsorship Mdm Li can save in the SNT account for the Government Matching Grant and a Great Eastern Cares Term Plan.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: Case Managers, who are social work-trained, will work with caregivers to craft personalised care plans and ensure funds are disbursed in accordance with these plans after caregivers have passed.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: With the Community Chest sponsorship, Mdm Li can start saving in the SNT account to benefit from the Government Matching Grant and use these savings to purchase a Great Eastern Cares Term Plan.

sections.label: Deaf access services study
sections.summary: In reply to Miss Rachel Ong's query, improvements to deaf access services, including training more Singapore Sign Language interpreters, are being studied.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: To Miss Rachel Ong's query, we are studying how to improve deaf access services, including training more Singapore Sign Language interpreters.

sections.label: CPF scheme and SNTC
sections.summary: The existing CPF Top-Up Matching Scheme and Special Needs Trust Company provide financial security for special needs families planning for the future.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: The existing CPF Top-Up Matching Scheme and Special Needs Trust Company are in place to provide financial security for special needs families, giving them a peace of mind in planning for the future.

sections.label: Taskforce input and refining
sections.summary: The speaker says they will keep listening and refining, thank Ms Denise Phua for her suggestions to the Taskforce, and will deliberate and share more when ready.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: And we will keep listening and we will keep refining.

sentences.speaker: The Senior Parliamentary Secretary to the Minister for Social and Family Development (Mr Eric Chua)
sentences.text: We thank Ms Denise Phua for her suggestions to the Taskforce, and we will deliberate over her input and share more when ready.

sections.label: Benefits for all citizen children
sections.summary: Subsidies for education, healthcare and the CDA are given to all citizen children regardless of parents' marital status.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Benefits that support their growth and development, such as subsidies for education, healthcare, and the CDA, are given to all citizen children, regardless of their parents’ marital status.

sections.label: Family counselling, parental leave, resilience
sections.summary: Family counselling capacity will double by 2030, paid parental leave rises to 30 weeks from April 2026, and over 85% of families reported moderate to high resilience.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Minister Masagos has also shared that we will double our family counselling capacity under the Strengthening Families Programme (FAM) by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: To provide better support for caregivers, we have significantly enhanced leave provisions for parents of newborns, increased mandatory paternity leave, and introduced a new Shared Parental Leave scheme, and in total, parents now have up to 30 weeks of paid parental leave from April 2026 onwards.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: MSF's latest survey findings show that more than 85% of Singaporean families reported moderate to high family resilience scores, reflecting good ability to bounce back from life’s challenges.

sections.label: Free LPA Form 1 filing
sections.summary: Filing Form 1 of the Lasting Power of Attorney will be free of charge for citizens.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Yesterday, I was very glad to share that we will make it free of charge for citizens to file Form 1 of the Lasting Power of Attorney (LPA).

sections.label: Preschool places and accessibility
sections.summary: Full-day preschool places rose from around 135,000 to over 220,000, enough nationally for resident children aged three and above, with 80% in Government-supported preschools.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: To ensure accessibility to preschools, we have increased the number of full-day preschool places from around 135,000 to now more than 220,000 in the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We now have enough full-day preschool places nationally for every resident child aged three and above.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We have also achieved our commitment of ensuring that 80% of preschoolers can have a place in a Government-supported preschool.

sections.label: Reduced full-day childcare fees
sections.summary: Full-day childcare fees are capped at $610 at Anchor Operator and $650 at Partner Operator preschools, a 15% reduction since 2020.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Since the start of the year, full-day childcare fees have been further reduced to a maximum of $610 at Anchor Operator preschools and $650 at Partner Operator preschools, a reduction of 15% since 2020.

sections.label: Higher income ceiling for subsidies
sections.summary: From January 2027, the gross monthly household income ceiling for Additional Subsidy and Kindergarten Fee Assistance rises to $15,000.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: From January 2027, we will raise the gross monthly household income ceiling for the Additional Subsidy for childcare and Kindergarten Fee Assistance Scheme to $15,000.

sections.label: Growing early education workforce
sections.summary: Attracting and retaining quality educators remains a priority, with 3,500 more early education educators to be added by 2030.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Attracting and retaining quality educators remains a priority for us.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We will grow our early education workforce by another 3,500 educators by 2030 to meet sector needs.

sections.label: Reviewing educator working conditions
sections.summary: Educators' working conditions and workload are being reviewed, with a sector-wide job redesign project and a refreshed Industry Digital Plan 2.0 with IMDA.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Together with operators and educators, we are currently reviewing educators' working conditions and workload, such as better enabling non-contact time.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We will also embark on a sector-wide job redesign project to review the job scopes, the work processes and support structures in our preschools and to improve work experiences.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: As shared by Minister Masagos yesterday, we will refresh the Industry Digital Plan 2.0 jointly with IMDA to enhance support for all preschools' digital transformation efforts, including non-Government-supported preschools.

sections.label: Families for Life community activities
sections.summary: MSF's partnerships with community partners enabled over 670 family-centric activities across all 24 towns last year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Through the strong partnerships that MSF has built with our community partners to run our Families for Life @ Community initiative, we were able to organise more than 670 family-centric activities across all 24 towns in Singapore last year.

sections.label: Taskforce on supporting PwDs
sections.summary: Suggestions and recommendations for supporting PwDs will be considered, and the Taskforce will complement the Enabling Masterplan 2030 and go beyond its recommendations.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: As Senior Parliamentary Secretary Eric has shared, we will carefully consider these suggestions, along with recommendations for supporting PwDs that many other Members have raised through the past week.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: I am grateful to be leading this Taskforce which will complement our Enabling Masterplan 2030 and go beyond its recommendations to provide greater opportunities and assurances of dignity and stability for them.

sections.label: Employment and care for PwDs
sections.summary: Employment opportunities tapping on PwDs' strengths will be grown, and day activity centres and sheltered workshops expanded to shorten waiting times.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We will grow employment opportunities that tap on their strengths.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: We will expand capacities of our day activity centres and sheltered workshops to provide stable and secure care environment for more clients and to shorten waiting times, thereby reducing the unnecessary stressful transitions for PwDs and their families.

sections.label: Taskforce report and PwD investment
sections.summary: The Taskforce's report will be released later this year, and the Government stands ready to invest more to support PwDs and their families.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The Taskforce's report will be released later this year.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: The Government stands ready to invest more to support PwDs and their families.

sections.label: Preschool places increase
sections.summary: Preschool places rose from 130,000 to 220,000 over the past decade.

sentences.speaker: The Minister of State for Social and Family Development (Mr Goh Pei Ming)
sentences.text: Over the past decade, preschool places have increased from 130,000 to 220,000 today.

sections.label: SNT Account setup funding
sections.summary: Families setting up an SNT Account will receive $5,000 initial capital through ComChest Funding.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Second, on families who are looking to set up the SNT Account, for these families, we will provide the initial $5,000 capital needed to set up an SNT Account through ComChest Funding.

sections.label: Social health integration trial
sections.summary: The social health integration trial involved about 500 families last year and is trialled in three SSO clusters, with health information shared with family coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Last year was the trial for the social health integration and about 500 families were involved.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In terms of where the regions will be trialled in, we are trialing in SSO clusters in: one, Bukit Batok, Bukit Panjang and Choa Chu Kang; two, Sembawang and Woodlands; and three, Tampines, Pasir Ris and Punggol.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In terms of the data sharing, MSF works closely with MOH, and the health care clusters so the relevant health information, like the children's mandatory immunisation records would be shared via a system interface with the family coaches.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: The family coach works together with the families, closely with the families who express interest to come on board the pilot and it is a very recent thing, the pilot was just in January, we aim for 100 families.

sections.label: Preschool educators workload policy
sections.summary: The workloads of preschool educators are heavy and long, and a policy is being worked on, starting with a parent-preschool charter.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: In fact, in the preschool sector, we recognise the importance of having this.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We agree, the workloads of our preschool educators are very heavy, the hours are very long, and this is a policy that we are working now.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We want to formalise this, and we are starting with the co-creation of a parent-preschool charter.

sections.label: Protected time for preschool educators
sections.summary: Six preschool closure days, Teachers' Day and Children's Day holidays in 2024, and no Saturday services since last year were designated.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: But of course, this requires time and we are studying and, we have in the past, set aside more protected time for them.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We designated six preschool closure days – development days, actually – to allow the centre, not only for personal training but also team training.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We have also designated Teachers' Day and Children's Day as holidays in 2024, we have also ceased childcare services or early childhood education services on Saturdays from last year onwards.

sections.label: Anchor Operator funding model
sections.summary: ECDA shifted Anchor Operator funding from a centre-capacity model to a per child funding model earlier in 2025.

sentences.speaker: Mr Kenneth Tiong Boon Kiat (Aljunied)
sentences.text: One, ECDA itself shifted Anchor Operator funding from a centre-capacity model to a per child funding model earlier in 2025.

sections.label: Enrolment-based preschool funding shift
sections.summary: Funding moved from capacity-based to enrolment-based to assign resources more equitably to all centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, to the Member's first question on whether per child funding should be extended to all centres.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: We moved from capacity-based to enrolment-based funding, primarily because we wanted to be more equitable to ensure that efficient resources are being assigned to all centres and if the centre is not full, we should not be assigning it based on capacity.

sections.label: Access to government-supported preschools
sections.summary: MSF and ECDA prioritise accessible, affordable, quality preschools, with 80% of preschoolers enrolled in Government-supported preschools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: MSF and ECDA's priority is to ensure that families have access to accessible, affordable, quality preschools and today, 80% of all preschoolers are able to enrol in Government-supported preschools.

sections.label: Anchor and Partner Operator selection
sections.summary: The Anchor and Partner Operator schemes use a rigorous selection process to evaluate private operators.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The operator schemes, the Anchor and Partner Operator schemes, employ a very rigorous selection process, and these are private operators that we are evaluating, so as to find out who are the best able to advance our early childhood objectives.

sections.label: Partner Operator selection factors
sections.summary: Partner Operator selection is competitive and considers track record, financial sustainability, accessibility and local preschooler demand.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: The Partner Operator selection is competitive and factors, such as track record in delivering services, financial sustainability, accessibility of the centres as well as the local preschooler demand in the immediate area where the preschool is located.

sections.label: Enabling Skills for Life Programme
sections.summary: The Enabling Skills for Life Programme includes an individual curriculum and development plan created with caregivers and PwDs.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Just want to highlight a few examples, so that we can illustrate the point.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: I have mentioned briefly in my speech that the Enabling Skills for Life Programme, an important component, is the individual curriculum and development plan, for which the caregivers, as well as the PwD themselves are very intimately and closely involved in the creation of the content and the milestones within.

sections.label: FAM centres family counselling
sections.summary: There are currently 11 FAM centres across Singapore providing family counselling services.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Mr Chairman, there are currently 11 FAM centres across Singapore providing family counselling services.

sections.label: Counsellor qualifications in FAM
sections.summary: FAM counsellors need tertiary qualifications in counselling, psychology or social work and at least three years' family experience.

sentences.speaker: Mr Goh Pei Ming
sentences.text: Counsellors in FAM are required to have the relevant tertiary qualifications in counselling, psychology or social work, along with a minimum of three years of experience working with families.

sections.label: Job Redesign Grant and ESH rollout
sections.summary: The Job Redesign Grant can be applied for under the Open Door Programme, and more ESHs are planned across the island.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: Under the existing Open Door Programme, there is a Job Redesign Grant that can already be applied for, so that is one potential avenue that we can point to.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: On her suggestion for the lighter version of the ESH – the ESH Minus or the ESH Portable – we are very keen to roll out more ESHs over different parts of the island in the coming years, so please stay tuned for more information.

sections.label: Pilot integration and queue pressure
sections.summary: A pilot integration could help the pressure valve queue of an average of six months.

sentences.speaker: Mr Cai Yinzhou (Bishan-Toa Payoh)
sentences.text: A pilot integration could help the pressure valve queue of an average of six months.

sections.label: ComLink+ outcomes and Progress Package
sections.summary: A 2025 MSF report showed positive employment and housing signs for ComLink+ families, and higher enrolment and attendance for children in the Progress Package.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Bearing in mind that ComLink+ was only launched in the middle of 2023, and if one looks at the MSF release paper in 2025 "Supporting Lower Income Household Trends", that report showed positive signs in some domains, like employment and housing, compared to the year before, experienced by families who had been enrolled in ComLink+.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: Children in ComLink+ Progress Package also had higher enrolment and attendance rates, compared to the children who were not emplaced.

sections.label: Tracking packages with academics
sections.summary: Academics are working with the speaker to study the packages' impact on families' short- and long-term outcomes.

sentences.speaker: Mr Zhulkarnain Abdul Rahim
sentences.text: In terms of tracking, we are also working with academics to study the impact of the packages on the families' short- and long-term outcomes.

sections.label: DAC clients and independent living
sections.summary: DACs support PwDs with moderate to more severe needs, many young and from SPED schools, focusing on readiness for independent community living.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: DACs are actually meant to support PwDs with moderate to more severe needs and in fact, the profile of clients in DACs are actually rather young, with many of them coming straight from SPED schools.

sentences.speaker: Mr Eric Chua
sentences.text: The focus really is on equipping and getting these clients ready for independent living in the community, but we acknowledge his suggestion and we will take it back to take a closer look.
